title: H-1B Visa Wage Gap Widens as DOL Data Reveals Which Employers Pay the Most
excerpt: A new Department of Labor analysis of over 3 million visa applications exposes stark salary disparities across H-1B employers, with tech giants like Roku, Netflix, and Nvidia paying well above the national median of $123,828.
body:
• The nationwide median H-1B salary stands at $123,828, but top tech employers like Roku ($376,579) and Netflix pay more than double that figure
  • The DOL's proposed rule would raise prevailing wage floors by 20-33%, adding an estimated $14,000 per worker per year — a potential $6.6 billion annual transfer to H-1B employees
  • India-born workers account for roughly 71% of H-1B approvals, and the new wage-weighted lottery system favors higher-paid applicants with 4x better selection odds

New analyses of Department of Labor filings and a proposed federal rule have thrown a sharp light on the salary landscape for H-1B visa workers in the United States — revealing that while some employers pay well above the national average, the majority of visa holders remain clustered in the program's two lowest wage tiers.

According to a Manifest Law analysis of DOL data, the nationwide median H-1B salary now stands at $123,828. California leads all states at $167,534, driven by Silicon Valley's concentration of tech employers. But individual companies show far wider variation: Roku tops the charts with a median H-1B salary of $376,579 — more than triple the national figure — while Netflix, Airbnb, LinkedIn, and Nvidia also rank among the highest-paying sponsors.

The Two-Tier Problem

Despite those headline numbers, the DOL's own data tells a different story for the majority of H-1B workers. According to the agency's March 2026 proposed rulemaking, 63% of certified Labor Condition Applications in fiscal year 2024 were filed at Wage Level I or Level II — the program's two lowest tiers, pegged at the 17th and 34th percentiles of local wages.

The average prevailing wage across all LCAs was $111,717, while employers actually offered $121,908 on average — a $10,191 premium. But the OEWS mean wage for equivalent occupations and geographies was $130,219, roughly $19,000 above what the current prevailing wage system requires.

"The average wage offered to H-1B workers was approximately $10,191 lower than the OEWS average wage for similarly classified occupations."

— Department of Labor, March 2026 NPRM

A 2023 Economic Policy Institute study, cited by the DOL, found that the top 30 H-1B employers laid off at least 85,000 workers in 2022 and early 2023 while simultaneously hiring 34,000 H-1B workers — fueling criticism that some firms use the visa program to cut labor costs rather than fill genuine talent gaps.

Big Tech's Spending Power

Among the largest H-1B users, Amazon ranked first with 13,265 approved applicants in 2025, followed by Meta and then Microsoft with 6,258 approvals, according to federal data compiled by Boundless Immigration. Goldman Sachs filed over 12,000 LCAs across its entities with an average salary around $134,000, while McKinsey, Morgan Stanley, and Hewlett Packard Enterprise averaged between $148,000 and $160,000.

Indian IT outsourcing firms present a contrasting picture. Companies like Hexaware Technologies ($94,375 average), Mindtree ($94,359), and Mphasis ($96,461) filed thousands of LCAs at salaries well below the national median — a pattern that the new weighted lottery system is designed to penalize.

DOL's Proposed Overhaul

The DOL's proposed rule, published on March 27, would raise the four prevailing wage levels from the 17th, 34th, 50th, and 67th percentiles to the 34th, 52nd, 70th, and 88th percentiles, respectively. For entry-level workers at Wage Level I, that translates to a 33% jump in the minimum required salary.

The agency estimates the change would cost employers an average of $14,000 more per worker per year, totaling up to $6.6 billion annually, rising to $9.3 billion once fully phased in around Year 6. About 22.5% of current LCA positions already pay above the proposed new floors and would be unaffected.

The Weighted Lottery's Early Impact

Separately, a new wage-weighted H-1B lottery introduced in the 2026 cycle is already reshaping selection patterns. Data from Boundless Immigration's report on the cycle shows that 68% of Level III and 64% of Level IV applicants were selected, compared to just 40% for Level I and 36% for Level II — a stark contrast to the previous random lottery.

"All of a sudden it has turned from a crapshoot of being able to stay in this country to an expectation that you can stay in this country if you're at a certain wage level."

— Xiao Wang, CEO of Boundless Immigration

Combined with the new $100,000 per-application fee for overseas hires, the changes are creating what Boundless describes as a structural shift toward higher-wage roles. In King County, Washington — home to Amazon and Microsoft — the gap between a prevailing-wage software engineer salary ($117,000) and a Level IV salary ($212,000) illustrates the incentive employers now have to inflate offers to boost lottery odds.

What It Means for Indian Professionals

Indian-born workers account for roughly 71% of H-1B approvals in recent years, making them the group most directly affected by these wage reforms. For highly skilled professionals already commanding top-tier salaries, the new weighted lottery is a net positive — better odds replace the old random draw. But for early-career workers and those employed by outsourcing firms at lower wage levels, the path to an H-1B has narrowed considerably.

The $100,000 application fee is proving particularly burdensome for rural hospitals trying to recruit doctors and nurses, and for startups founded by Indian-born entrepreneurs recruiting from their networks, according to industry observers.

What's Next

The DOL's proposed wage rule is in a 60-day public comment period. The agency is also considering an alternative "experience benchmarking" approach that would set wages based on the actual education and experience of the sponsored worker, using the 50th, 62nd, 75th, and 90th percentiles. If finalized, the new prevailing wages would apply only to new LCA filings, leaving existing approvals untouched. Employers planning H-1B filings are advised to model their wage exposure now, as the final rule could land before the FY 2028 filing season.
